content: Measuring model load and token decoding separately is critical for a local GPU runtime because these phases have fundamentally different resource profiles and bottlenecks: model loading is primarily I/O and memory-bandwidth-bound (moving weights from disk to VRAM), while token decoding is compute-bound (matrix multiplications and attention operations). By isolating these metrics, developers can accurately diagnose performance issues—such as slow disk reads or insufficient VRAM bandwidth during load versus inefficient kernel execution or memory access patterns during inference—and optimize each stage independently, ensuring that the total time-to-first-token and subsequent tokens-per-second are maximized without conflating distinct hardware constraints.
